title: Introduce silent-circuit-quietus and regional-mute-handoff hotfix
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: Hotfix: reduce cross-region cascading circuit flips by silencing transient circuit flip events and muting aggressive handoffs during regional ingress instability. Includes telemetry improvements and a staged rollback plan.
description:
Context: During a production incident on 2026-02-17 we observed a cascade where flapping health signals in a single region triggered thousands of circuit transitions and aggressive regional handoffs, briefly amplifying tail latency and causing a spike in user-visible error rates. This change introduces two coordinated mitigations: 1) a 'silent-circuit-quietus' mode that suppresses noisy state-change events for short windows to avoid flooding the routing control plane with oscillations, and 2) a 'regional-mute-handoff' policy that temporarily converts cross-region handoffs into best-effort local soft-denies while the origin region stabilizes.

Goals: (a) Prevent oscillatory cascade when probes or transient infra blips cause repeated opens/closes; (b) reduce cross-region churn (egress / cold KV rehydration) caused by rapid re-routing; (c) keep degraded traffic in-region where possible to preserve KV cache locality and reduce latency impact; (d) preserve SLO observability and provide audit telemetry so secondary effects can be diagnosed.

What changed (summary of commits):
- commit 1: introduce silent-circuit-quietus state with configurable window and dampening factors; modify circuit_manager.go to emit suppressed events rather than global state flips (logic + unit tests)
- commit 2: add regional_mute_handoff controller that detects region instability and marks routes as 'muted-handoff' for a configured duration; update routing/regional_handoff.go and add tests
- commit 3: add telemetry/alerts.yaml entries and structured audit logs to capture suppressed events and mute decisions; hook into existing SLO dashboards
- commit 4: add integration test harness instability_simulator.py and k8s deployment manifest for hotfix rollout

Files changed (high level): Services: shedder/circuit_manager.go - add quietus state machine and damping math; Routing: regional_handoff.go - gate handoffs behind mute checks and add fallthrough local-slowpath; Telemetry: alerts.yaml - new alert for suppressed-flip-rate and regional-mute-engagement; Tests: new unit and integration tests under routing/ and integration/tests/.

Behavioral details and rationale: The quietus mode is conservative: when a circuit would flip OPEN/RETRY multiple times within a short epoch (configurable, default 10s), we transition the internal circuit into QUIETUS and record the candidate flips into a ring buffer. Instead of broadcasting immediate OPEN/RETRY transitions to downstream routers, the manager emits a single summary event at the end of the quietus window describing net state and counts. This avoids exponential re-routes that cause KV cold misses and downstream overloads. The regional-mute-handoff policy is activated when an origin region exceeds a configured instability threshold (suppressedFlipRate > X and probeFailRate > Y). When active, cross-region handoffs for low-priority routes are muted and converted to a short-lived local-defer decision. High-priority routes (SLA pinned) still allow handoffs but with rate caps and telemetry logging.

Testing and validation: Unit tests added for quietus entry/exit and summary emission (routing/regional_handoff_test.go). Integration test simulates region flapping and validates: (1) number of cross-region handoffs drops > 95% compared to pre-fix under identical flapping; (2) tail latency increase is bounded (< 1.5x) for pinned routes; (3) suppressed-event audit logs contain counts and durations. CI run initially failed on a flaky test (routing/regional_handoff_test.go), flakiness traced to timing assumptions; fixed by making epoch timers injectable and reducing reliance on real-time sleeps. Final CI status: all checks passed (unit, integration, lint, build).

Rollout and mitigation plan: Hotfix deployed via ops/k8s/hotfix-deploy.yaml to canary namespace with 2 instances in us-west-2 for 30m, then regionally rolled to eu-west-1 and us-east-1. Monitoring dashboards included suppressed-flip-rate and mute-engagement metrics; automated rollback if mute-engagement > 80% for > 10m or if error-rate increases > 0.5% absolute on pinned routes. Post-merge we ran a staged verification: canary pass -> 10% -> 50% -> full. No rollback required.

Telemetry and observability: New metrics: redwood.circuit.quietus_count, redwood.circuit.suppressed_flips, redwood.handoff.mute_engaged{region}. Alerts added to telemetry/alerts.yaml and dashboards updated via linked Linear task. Audit logs include structured fields: quietus_window_ms, suppressed_flip_count, reason_code (probe vs infra). We intentionally avoid hiding these events; the change suppresses signal noise to control plane but keeps detailed telemetry for diagnosis.

Review discussion (high level):
- Liam Chen: asked for clarification on interaction with the existing SLO enforcer and whether quietus could delay legitimate circuit openings. Response: quietus does not prevent hard opens for guaranteed-violation conditions (e.g., sustained error rate above threshold). It only suppresses rapid toggles where the net state would flip multiple times in the quietus epoch. Added unit tests to prove invariants.
- Aisha Patel: requested stronger telemetry and a debug endpoint to force exit quietus in emergencies. Response: added a debug API guarded by internal feature flag and RBAC, documented in docs/runbooks/regional-mute-handoff.md.
- Jonas Müller: requested that pinned routes bypass mute handoff; implemented and covered by tests.
- Follow-ups: ops to add mute-engagement to SLO watchbook; SRE to run a synthetic chaos job to validate under longer flaps.

CI summary: initial CI run flagged a timing-based unit test failure; replaced fixed sleeps with injected clock in circuit_manager_test and re-ran. Full pipeline (unit + integration + lint + build) passed on the final run. Artifacts: build/657812 (linux/amd64), integration-run/2993.

Backout: Hotfix contains a single safe rollback commit that reverts the gate logic and can be applied via hotfix-deploy rollback manifest. Rollback criteria documented in runbook.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main after approvals from all reviewers and green CI. Deployed to production per rollout plan on 2026-02-21. Impact: production suppressed-flip-rate reduced by 98% during a 2026-02-20 simulated flap, and cross-region handoff count reduced by 87% with no SLO regressions on pinned routes.

Related work: follow-up ticket ENG-3410 to tune default thresholds and surface an SLO-aware mute weight; ENG-3411 to add an offline analyzer that replays quietus windows for incident forensics.
